questions.def: Possessive 'whose' shows the book belongs to the author.
questions.question: The author, ___ book I read last year, is giving a lecture.

questions.def: 'Where' indicates a place; the restaurant.
questions.question: That's the restaurant ___ we had dinner last week.

questions.def: 'Living' is a reduced relative clause functioning as an adjective.
questions.question: The people ___ next door are very friendly.

questions.def: 'That' introduces a defining relative clause.
questions.question: This is the same problem ___ we faced last year.

questions.def: 'Why' introduces a relative clause of reason.
questions.question: The reason ___ I'm calling is to confirm the meeting.

questions.def: 'Who's' should be 'whose', indicating possession.
questions.question: She's the artist who's work is exhibited in several galleries now.

questions.def: 'Informed' is a reduced passive relative clause.
questions.question: The clients ___ of the changes are happy.

questions.def: 'Which' introduces non-defining relative clauses.
questions.question: The package, ___ arrived yesterday, was damaged.

questions.def: 'Whom' is the object of the preposition 'about'.
questions.question: He's the colleague ___ I told you about.

questions.def: 'What' should be 'which' in a non-defining clause.
questions.question: The book, what I found interesting, was about history.

questions.def: 'Seen' is a reduced relative clause functioning as an adjective.
questions.question: The movie ___ last night was amazing.

questions.def: 'When' refers to a time; the day.
questions.question: The day ___ I met her was unforgettable.

questions.def: 'Whose' indicates possession of the roof.
questions.question: The house, ___ roof is red, is very old.

questions.def: 'Which' should be 'who' when referring to a person.
questions.question: She's the person which helped me with my project.

questions.def: 'Published' is a reduced passive relative clause.
questions.question: The articles ___ in the journal are peer-reviewed.

questions.def: 'Where' refers to a place; the city.
questions.question: The city ___ he was born is beautiful.

questions.def: 'That' is used after 'the only thing'.
questions.question: The only thing ___ matters is your health.

questions.def: 'Selected' is a reduced passive relative clause.
questions.question: The candidates ___ for the interview will be notified.

questions.def: 'Whom' is the object of the verb 'saw'.
questions.question: She's the woman ___ I saw at the conference.

questions.def: 'That' is often used in spoken English instead of 'which/whom'.
questions.question: That's the book ___ I was telling you about.

questions.def: 'Invited' is a reduced passive relative clause.
questions.question: The guests ___ to the party are arriving soon.

questions.def: 'Whose' shows possession; integrity belongs to the person.
questions.question: He's a person ___ integrity is beyond question.

questions.def: 'Whose' shows possession; the deadline belongs to the project.
questions.question: The project, ___ deadline is next week, is progressing well.

questions.def: 'Which' should be 'whom' (or 'that') when referring to a person.
questions.question: She's the doctor which I trust completely with my health.

questions.def: 'Written' is a reduced passive relative clause.
questions.question: The essay ___ by her was very insightful.

questions.def: 'Where' refers to a place; the restaurant.
questions.question: The restaurant ___ he works is very famous.

questions.def: 'That' is commonly used instead of 'which/whom'.
questions.question: This is the book ___ everyone is talking about.

questions.def: "Which" is used for non-restrictive relative clauses referring to things.
questions.question: The book, ___ I borrowed from you, was excellent.

questions.def: "Whose" shows possession, connecting the artist to their painting.
questions.question: The artist ___ painting was stolen is devastated.

questions.def: "Who" should be "whom" as it's the object of "thought".
questions.question: The man who I thought was the manager wasn't.
